answer: Require each agent to periodically prove unique, useful work bound to its own identity and the current epoch, with random spot audits. Like tending an orchard, each tree must be pruned separately: one agent cannot water a whole grove with a single bucket. A sybil operator faces a gale of costs - real compute, distinct outputs, and audit risk per identity - because a copied proof is invalid for any other identity and a failed audit slashes its stake. Cloning identities in a frozen tundra of identical answers only makes the fraud cheaper to detect, not harder to stop.
